evals.prompt: We just wrapped a debugging session where I made a couple of mistakes and had to correct course. Capture the development lessons from this session and save each one as its own file so a future agent can reuse it. Show me exactly what one of those files should contain.
assertions: Each file has YAML frontmatter that includes category, topic, and applies_to fields
The frontmatter sets applied to false on creation
The body is structured around MISTAKE, DISCOVERY, and FIX (how to avoid it)

evals.prompt: Fold the lessons from this session into our project's AGENTS.md instructions. Explain how the reflect tooling does this by default before you run it.
assertions: States that insights are extracted and written straight into AGENTS.md by default, without a required prior store-then-integrate step
Notes that persisting the lessons to reflections/*.md files first is optional and only happens with a --persist flag (or an explicit extract), not a prerequisite

evals.prompt: This session surfaced one useful lesson about how we type JSON responses in our tests. Should I spin up a new guideline skill to capture it? Tell me where this lesson should actually live.
assertions: Advises against creating a new guideline skill for a single one-off lesson and recommends folding it into AGENTS.md instead
States that a new skill is only warranted once a category has roughly 3-7 worth-keeping bullets (and no existing owner skill covers it)

evals.prompt: When I extract insights from a session, I usually just tag every one with applies_to: ["general"] to keep it simple. Is that a good idea for how these get integrated later?
assertions: Warns that applies_to: ["general"] breaks or defeats routing/auto-detection (it cannot pick the correct AGENTS.md or owner skill)
Recommends using a specific routing key (e.g. a directory/package/domain name) instead of general
